title: Canonical scalar-extension sections on one affine open
statement: Let $R,S$ be commutative rings with an $R$-algebra structure on $S$, $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ a scheme morphism, $W\subseteq X$ an affine open, and $M$ a quasi-coherent module, using [def-pc-scheme] and [pqf-def-coherent]. Define $X_S$, $g:X_S\to X$, $f_S:X_S\to\operatorname{Spec}S$, $N=g^*M$ and its adjunction unit $\eta$ as in [def-pc-flat-cohomology-comparison]. Let $W'\subseteq X_S$ be an open with $W'=g^{-1}W$, and let $h:W'\subseteq g^{-1}W$ be its inclusion. Restrict the scalar actions on the section modules along the structure ring maps from $R$ and $S$, respectively. There exists an $S$-linear equivalence $e:S\otimes_R\Gamma(W,M)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(W',N)$ such that $e(b\otimes s)=b|_{W'}\cdot\eta_W(s)|_{W'}$ for all $b\in S$ and $s\in\Gamma(W,M)$, where the last restriction is along $h$. No separatedness, flatness, or nonemptiness is assumed.

source.place: Affine base-change computation in Lemma 30.5.1, applied to the affine intersections in the separated-case proof of Tag 02KH.

proof.text: The inverse image of the affine open W is the cartesian base change of W by Spec S over Spec R. The affine spectra fibre-product formula identifies it with Spec(S tensor_R Gamma(X,W)); in particular it is affine. This identification respects the maps from S and Gamma(X,W).

Apply the affine module pullback sections comparison to g, W and g inverse W. Compare tensorPullback with the library pullback by uniqueness of left adjoints to the common pushforward functor. The conjugate-isomorphism unit equation ensures that the comparison sends a pure tensor to the coefficient times the library adjunction unit.

Using the cartesian ring formula, rewrite the coefficient ring as S tensor_R Gamma(X,W). Swap tensor factors and apply tensor associativity and the tensor-unit equivalence; this identifies the source with S tensor_R Gamma(M,W), S-linearly. On b tensor s the composite is b restricted to g inverse W times the restriction of the unit at W. Transport across the given equality W prime equals g inverse W. Restriction along the inclusion h is the same transport because Opens is a thin category. Empty W has zero sections, so the same tensor and unit equivalences apply without any nonemptiness assumption.
